title: DSA: Stacks (LIFO)
description: A Stack is a linear data structure that follows the LIFO (Last-In-First-Out) principle. This means the last element inserted is the first one removed. Common operations include 'push' (add) and 'pop' (remove). Stacks are used in function calls, undo mechanisms, and expression parsing.
example:
# Stack Implementation using List
stack = []

# Push
stack.append('a')
stack.append('b')

# Pop
print(stack.pop()) # 'b'

# Peek (Last element)
print(stack[-1]) # 'a'

challenges.title: LIFO Concept
challenges.exercise: Print 'Last-In-First-Out' to confirm you understand the stack principle.
